prerequisites.reason: Line and surface formulas are computed by ordinary and multiple integration; Green, Stokes, and divergence combine partial derivatives, Jacobian area scaling, and interior volume integrals with oriented boundaries.

recommended.reason: Covectors, alternating multilinear forms, and wedge products explain the closing generalized-Stokes interpretation. The concrete vector-calculus examples introduce their own line, surface, and flux formulas.

background: Elementary three-dimensional coordinate geometry and the cross product as an oriented parallelogram-area vector; a working component calculation may need separate review. Trigonometric curve parametrizations and basic one-variable substitution are assumed.
readiness_checks: Can you differentiate the circular path (cos t, sin t), calculate its speed, and distinguish a position from its velocity?
Can you set up an integral over a disk in polar coordinates with the radial area factor, and explain why an unsigned area formula uses the absolute Jacobian determinant?
Can you use the chain rule to express the derivative of f along a path as gradient f dotted with the path velocity, then integrate a scalar rate by endpoint subtraction?
